Comment: "HSF has a rather particular person-marking system compared with other Mayan languages: the languages of the Huastecan group use three different sets of person markers, not two as in the other Mayan languages. The person-marking system of HSF is not a typical ergative system but rather resembles an inverse system. The Huastecan languages have developed an atypical inverse system; these are the only Mayan languages that encode transitive person agreement in this way. Zavala (1993) published an extensive study of this problem." (our translation of the Spanish original)
